name: Lares Trek
region: Lares valley and Cordillera Urubamba, Calca, Cusco
why: From the hot springs of Lares through Quechua weaving villages and llama pastures, over a 4,500 m pass between glacier lakes, down to Patacancha above the Sacred Valley.
book: No permit needed. Agencies in Cusco run it with horses and a cook; the drive from Cusco to Lares over the Calca pass takes several hours. From Patacancha a colectivo goes down to Ollantaytambo and its railway station.
water: Streams and lakes (treat them: animals graze everywhere). Shops only in Lares and Patacancha.
dangers: The Ipsaycocha pass at about 4,450 m: acclimatise in Cusco first.
Frost at the Ipsaycocha camp; rain and hail in the afternoons.
Dogs at the farms along the way.
turnaround: Not at the foot of the pass climb above Huacahuasi by 11:00: camp in Huacahuasi and cross the next morning.

points.name: Lares hot springs
points.note: Day 1: the thermal pools just west of Lares village (3,200 m). The path follows the valley up past Tambohuaylla.

points.name: Huacahuasi
points.note: A weaving village at about 3,750 m: first camp, women selling textiles in front of stone houses.

points.name: Ipsaycocha pass
points.note: Day 2: the highest point, about 4,450 m (Abra Ipsay; some maps say 4,600 m), with glaciers above and the Ipsaycocha lakes below.

points.name: Laguna Ipsaycocha camp
points.note: The camp below the pass by the lake, under the ice of the Urubamba range. Cold night.

points.name: Patacancha
points.note: Day 3: down the valley to the weaving village at about 3,700 m; colectivos run on to Ollantaytambo.
